items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: the other one was Milt Fillius who was class of ’44

ctx.x: That’s the only side there was, that’s right.

You are the second Hamilton alum I’ve interviewed, the other one was Milt Fillius who was class of ’44. But I asked him and I’m going to ask you, I’ve always been impressed by the loyalty of a significant number of Hamilton alums. And is there a reason for that in your mind?

Well I surely agree with you, it’s remarkable. It was true in my case, I still have very close friendships with many of my classmates and yet both my sons went here, one class of ’88 and one class of ’90 and they have exactly the same friendships. And indeed those friends are now friends of my wife and I. We often on New Year’s Eve will get a call from a Lieutenant JG in Tokyo who is stationed there and is just calling us up to wish us a Happy New Year. And it’s a remarkable thing.
